description.value: The study examined fear conditioning and physiological-anatomical correlations in healthy controls, Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal lobar degeneration using skin conductance responses and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: We studied FC in controls (n = 25), Alzheimer's disease (n = 25) and FTLD (n = 25).

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional comparison of healthy controls, Alzheimer's disease and FTLD.

spans.text: The goal of the current study was to compare the effects of FTLD and Alzheimer's disease on FC, taking into account the basic processing underlying FC.

Most importantly, FC has been extensively studied in humans and animals, and appears to depend on the same brain structures across species, allowing parallel studies in humans and animals to be designed.

name.value: Across Groups — US reactivity (ROI: B/L ACC/OFC/amygdala)

spans.text: Reactivity to the US (average across the 10 presentations) was correlated with volume in dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) region (voxel-level P = 0.01) and left insula across the entire group (voxel-level P = 0.001) but these effects were not significant after multiple comparison correction.

value: Reactivity to the US was correlated with volume in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and left insula across the entire group, but these effects were not significant after multiple comparison correction.

name.value: Across Groups — Extinction (ROI: B/L posterior OFC)

label.value: Across the whole group of subjects

spans.text: Although this finding was significant across the whole group of subjects (after multiple comparison correction for an OFC ROI), the data looking at this relationship in individual groups suggested that most of the effect was driven by the normal control subjects, who were able to generate conditioned responses.

value: Extinction was correlated with volume in the posterior orbitofrontal cortex, with a more significant effect on the right; this finding was consistent with previous studies relating posterior orbitofrontal cortex to extinction and modification of previously established cue-reward associations.

name.value: Normal Control — US reactivity (ROI: B/L ACC/OFC/amygdala)

definition.value: US reactivity in the Normal Control group

spans.text: Although this finding was significant across the whole group of subjects (after multiple comparison correction for an OFC ROI), the data looking at this relationship in individual groups suggested that most of the effect was driven by the normal control subjects, who were able to generate conditioned responses.

value: In controls, US reactivity was more significantly correlated with dorsal anterior cingulate cortex volume; this association remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons within the frontal-temporal ROI.

name.value: Normal Control — Extinction (ROI: B/L posterior OFC)

definition.value: Extinction in the Normal Control group

spans.text: Although this finding was significant across the whole group of subjects (after multiple comparison correction for an OFC ROI), the data looking at this relationship in individual groups suggested that most of the effect was driven by the normal control subjects, who were able to generate conditioned responses.

value: In normal controls, the relationship between extinction and right posterior orbitofrontal cortex volume was not significant after multiple comparison correction.
In FTLD, conditioning was correlated with tissue content in the right amygdala, although the association was not significant after correction for the volume of the bilateral amygdala ROI.

definition.value: US reactivity in the FTLD group

value: In FTLD, reactivity to the US appeared to be correlated with volume in the left insula, but this was not significant after multiple comparison correction.

definition.value: Extinction in the Alzheimer's disease group

value: In Alzheimer's disease, the posterior orbitofrontal cortex effect was less significant and was not significant after multiple comparison correction.
